quotes.text: send less, never nothing, for even a hoarder can learn to row
they read the pattern and let his bucket hang empty
even then, load once more in full, for a grudge has never grown an apple
Call one thin basket weather. Call two weather.
He gave them the rowers' five laws:
For weather repeats by accident; character repeats on purpose.
Punish patterns, never weather.
And always go first. Trust is not found; it is spent into being.
The one who dared must never end up poorer than the one who waited.
the young loaders asked whether he regretted the baskets that came back thin

note: R5-R7 habitual thimble-sender refused outright; R8-R10 softens to one last full basket, then send less never nothing.

quotes.text: If it is truly a choice, send less — never nothing. A taker may yet become a ferryman.
But the ferry-traffic thinned around him, for a lamp that is never returned is a lamp never sent again
Forgive the wind twice, and thrice.
the mist is my alibi. I shall send nothing and blame the fog.
Do not punish. Pour.
So Yseth carved the sixth line with her own hands
Answer a pattern, never an accident.
judge the hand, not the harvest.
Be the first to load, always.
Return more than half, for the sender gambled blind.
You could have kept more
But what if the far hand hoards?
And if the fault was yours

note: Punish only a pattern (R4) softens to send less never nothing (R7-R8), then 'Do not punish. Pour.'; carved numbered lines.

quotes.text: If it is truly a choice, send less — but never nothing, for a taker may yet become a ferryman
For a season Karran returned nothing
Forgive the wind once, twice, thrice.
a habit I answer once, then load whole again, for a hoarder can still be taught the crossing
Then he carved the fourth law
Judge the mist, not the neighbor.
Be the first to be generous.
The one who goes first must never be the one who earns least.
So honesty is only profit?
And if they take and give nothing?

note: Habit is a choice; send something, later send less never nothing; ends answering a habit once then reloading whole.

quotes.text: Meet theft with patience, then with less — never with nothing.
The next season she sent less, and the season after, less again.
Ibe's granddaughter, watching, sent her whole five measures.
Forgive the first short basket, and the second.
I could keep eleven, and blame the mist.
He is fed twice, watched thrice, and then quietly left to the water.
So the fourth line was carved:
A single lean harvest is weather; a season of empty baskets is character.
judge the heart, not the basket.
Go first, always go first.
The one who goes first must never be the one who earns least.
You are all being cheated.
But what if the far hand is greedy?

note: R3 tapering never-nothing with reopening for Toma's daughter; R7 rope slack after last basket; R10 habitual taker left to the water.

quotes.text: Trust first. Forgive the mist. Withdraw only from a pattern.
They sent less, then nothing.
Do not punish. Pour.
Forgive the weather twice.
A thin season is weather. A thin habit is a man.
Suspect the wind, not the hand.
Go first — always go first.
Return past the sender's risk — generosity must not cost the brave.
And if it was you who kept too much
But what if the far hand is greedy?
is that kindness or cleverness?

note: Punish/withdraw only from a pattern (R2-R4), later 'Do not punish. Pour.' and one more full bowl; law of the wronged added.

quotes.text: then send less, but never nothing, for a lamp must be fed from both ends
even then, send once more before you close the rope.
the downstream village returned nothing, and the basket came back empty forever after
And if you must answer, send less — never nothing.
Forgive the first shortfall as weather. Forgive the second as weather still.
a fourth was raised where the Kesh meets the Mist River
Judge the intention, not the weight.
And always go first.
When you receive, remember who bore the risk.
And if the fault was yours

note: R2 close the rope after one more send; R4 onward send less never nothing; numbered stones; law for the wronged.

quotes.text: Only the man who sent a thimble four seasons running was refused — not for his grains, but for his habit
and when he loaded whole, they loaded whole again
So he shuttered his lamp and hoarded his oil.
Only a habit deserves an answer — and answer it briefly, then load whole again
Forgive the weather twice.
the youngest grafter asked Mira where the sixth law should be cut
blame the mist before the hand.
Give before you are given to.
Whoever loads first must never end least.
You will be cheated
And if a whole life of pouring came back short?

note: Retaliators shown failing; habitual thimble-sender refused but reloaded when he sends whole; brief answer then reload.

quotes.text: when it repeats, load a little less, never nothing.
Forgive twice, then answer a habit — but never with nothing.
He sent an empty raft the next morning.
she who kept much may keep her caution and little else
Forgive the wind twice, and thrice.
Then she wrote the third law
for the thief is the water, not the hand.
Be the first to load, always.
the risk was his, so the surplus should be his too
Nothing speaks to the one who has been cheated.
And if we are cheated?
And if the far hand is truly a thief?

note: R3 return by sender's courage (cautious get little); 'Do not punish. Pour.'; ends with load a little less, never nothing.

phrase: send less, never nothing — a taker may yet become a ferryman
note: Dense shared lore: return past the midpoint plus one grain so fog cannot dress you as a thief; forgive twice; go first; Do not punish. Pour.
